title: An orchestrator starts its lanes with no click from you
why: Your gripe, Oct 26 21:13 CDT (cmsg_01DoF7thf3iq2Srr1UsfXgh2MqbYDeMhgjWP54XKb1P71s, screenshot): the degen orchestrator on the Mac desktop app needed you to accept each of four sessions it started with start_session, even in Bypass permissions mode.
note: Goal: an orchestrator starts its lanes with no click from you. Step 1, Oct 27 (Mac, read-only): no allow rule, default mode or desktop setting covers mcp__ccd_session__start_session (settings.json, settings.local.json, managed settings and the desktop config checked); hooks/guard.py only denies a Haiku model or a full-load reading, so the card is not ours. Most likely the start_session call kind decides it: "offer" always shows the 'New session / Do it here' card, "user_asked" starts with none (unproven; one start with each kind shows it; brief briefs/c107-start-session-allow.md). Step 2, design call, triage's proposal: an orchestrator uses user_asked only for a lane you asked for or one c79 lets start without asking (safe follow-ups), and offer for anything else, so the kind never claims an ask you did not make; if user_asked still shows a card, lanes start as background subagents in their own worktrees and the orchestrate skill says so. Needs no answer; object and it changes. The opening question ("Start the JD, Duo, Pills and records sessions now?") is c79's. The Mac needs c119's fix to get any of it. Port: yes; global settings. Placed ahead of c93, after c103 (triage, Oct 27): every orchestrator on the Mac hits it.
ask:
# c107 step 1: what pre-approves start_session on the Mac desktop app?

Local liaison, Oct 27, against claude-settings main d4e1b86b. Mac session, read-only: no settings
edit, no session start, no ask to the owner. Print no token, cookie or key.

hooks/guard.py never asks on mcp__ccd_session__start_session, so the accept the owner clicked most
likely comes from the desktop app.

1. List every permissions rule (allow, ask, deny, defaultMode) in ~/.claude/settings.json,
   ~/.claude/settings.local.json and any managed settings that names ccd_session or mcp__.
2. List the setting names (not values that look secret) in the Claude desktop app's config under
   ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/ that touch permissions, approvals, or sessions.
3. From the Claude Code docs (code.claude.com/docs, permissions page), say whether an allow rule
   `mcp__ccd_session__start_session` pre-approves an MCP tool in bypass mode, and whether the
   desktop app's own session-start prompt is outside settings.json.
4. Report in 10 lines: what exists today, the most likely pre-approval (a rule or a desktop
   setting), and what one owner click would prove it.
